ENTJ>INTJ.title: Even after deciding, you go over it again at home.
ENTJ>INTJ.body: In front of people, you can decide quickly and keep the conversation moving. But you really firm up your thinking in quiet time alone. Even a plan that got decided in a discussion gets reordered by you alone once you're home, and you've sent it out by the next morning.
ENTJ>INTJ.say: "This is the overall plan. I'll send the details by tomorrow."
ENTJ>INTJ.do: When you're given a task, you count back from the deadline and decide what to do on which day.
ENTJ>INTJ.do_s: When you get an assignment, you count back from the deadline and decide what to do on which day.
ENTJ>INTJ.worry: You can decide in the meeting, but at home you keep thinking, "Was that okay?" When you see people day after day, you don't get enough time to rest your head.
ENTJ>INTJ.worry_s: You can decide in the group discussion, but at home you keep thinking, "Was that okay?" When you see people day after day, you don't get enough time to rest your head.
ENTJ>INTJ.karai: When you're put in charge of a trip, you send everyone a table that even has travel times.
ENTJ>INTJ.aru: In the meeting you can say, "We're going with this," but at home you're going over the same plan until midnight.
ENTJ>INTJ.aru_s: In the group project meeting you can say, "We're going with this," but at home you're going over the same plan until midnight.
ENTJ>INTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who gets energy from talking with people. Through all kinds of experiences, you picked up a way of doing things where you firm up your ideas in time alone. In front of people you focus on deciding, and you check the details once things are quiet. You can't relax about a plan you decided in front of people until you've calmly checked it alone for anything missing, which is why you end up going over it at home until midnight.
ENTJ>INTJ.yure: The question that makes you waver is "Do people give you energy, or do you need time alone?" It depends on whether you picture yourself running a meeting or fixing documents at night.
ENTJ>INTJ.yure_s: The question that makes you waver is "Do people give you energy, or do you need time alone?" It depends on whether you picture yourself leading the group discussion or fixing the presentation slides alone at night.
ENTJ>INTJ.plus: You can make decisions in front of people and finish things on your own, so your team can really count on you. Wanting time to think isn't selfish.
ENTJ>INTJ.tip: When you make plans to see people, keep the next evening free. If your rest day is already set, you can enjoy the day with people too.
ENTJ>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to sort out your thoughts by talking with people. Have you ever been explaining a stuck plan to someone and suddenly seen the answer? Talk to people earlier, and your work moves faster.
ENTJ>INTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to sort out your thoughts by talking with people. Have you ever been explaining a stuck plan to someone and suddenly seen the answer? Talk to people earlier, and your assignments and prep move faster.

ENTJ>INTP.title: After deciding, you ask yourself, "Really?"
ENTJ>INTP.body: You decide fast, but right away you start thinking, "But is that really right?" Even after something's settled, you go over it alone at night, and if you think of another way, the next day you say, "Mind if I change it a little?" You can decide quickly, and you can also think things through slowly.
ENTJ>INTP.say: "It's decided, but let me hear one other option first."
ENTJ>INTP.do: With big news stories, you read a few articles to check if they're true.
ENTJ>INTP.worry: Even when you want to decide quickly, the more you think, the more other answers you see, and you get stuck. You try to fit in both days out with people and days thinking alone, and you pack your schedule until it wears you out.
ENTJ>INTP.karai: You check so many comparison sites before buying an appliance that you know more than the salesperson by the time you get to the store.
ENTJ>INTP.karai_s: You check so many comparison sites before buying earbuds that you know more than the salesperson by the time you get to the store.
ENTJ>INTP.aru: Five minutes after saying, "OK, that's decided," you flip it yourself: "Actually, maybe not."
ENTJ>INTP.why: By nature, you're the type who wants to decide in front of people and keep going. Through experience, you also learned to keep thinking on your own and leave the answer open. Even when you've already said what you decided, your head hasn't stopped thinking. When a different angle pops up right after you decide, you can't help checking it, and five minutes later you've reversed your own decision.
ENTJ>INTP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on "Do people give you energy?" and "Plan ahead or go with the moment?" The result depends on whether you answer picturing yourself leading people or looking things up.
ENTJ>INTP.plus: You rethink even after deciding because you're really looking for a better answer. Thanks to that, you run into fewer problems later.
ENTJ>INTP.tip: Once you decide, tell people first: "I won't change this for a week." Once you've told people, you won't flip it right away.
ENTJ>INTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to gather people and get things moving fast. It shows when a discussion stalls and you can't help saying, "OK, let's do this." Use it, and your ideas turn into reality faster.

ENTJ>ENTJ.title: Once the goal is set, the steps come to you right away.
ENTJ>ENTJ.body: Once a goal is set, the order of what needs doing takes shape in your head right away. While everyone is looking at each other asking, "What should we do?", you've already written out who does what and by when, and handed it out. That's how you end up being the organizer without noticing. In places where nothing gets decided, you tend to wear out.
ENTJ>ENTJ.say: "So what do you want in the end?"
ENTJ>ENTJ.do: Even on days off you decide, "Shopping in the morning, gym in the afternoon," and feel good when it goes that way.
ENTJ>ENTJ.worry: You move at your own pace and only later notice others haven't kept up. You want even rest to have a purpose, so it's hard to relax.
ENTJ>ENTJ.karai: Even on a day you said you'd take it easy, you've finished three errands by noon.
ENTJ>ENTJ.aru: When a trip comes up with friends, you're the one deciding where to go and when to meet. When everyone's unsure, you can't help saying, "OK, let's do this."
ENTJ>ENTJ.why: Both what you were born with and what you learned through experience are about looking ahead and deciding among people. Since you were little, the deciding role has tended to land on you, and each time you felt, "Once it's decided, everyone can move." Those experiences added up, and now time spent hesitating feels like a waste. Even while everyone else is unsure, the order is already worked out in your head, so saying "Okay, let's do this" first feels more natural than waiting quietly.
ENTJ>ENTJ.yure: You're likely to get nearly the same result every time you take the test. If a different one shows up, you may have been worn out and low on social energy, or going through a stretch of matching other people's pace.
ENTJ>ENTJ.plus: You decide first because you don't want to waste anyone's time. Because you decide, the people around you don't have to waste time unsure.
ENTJ>ENTJ.tip: On trips, let your friends choose just the dinner spot. You'll end up somewhere you wouldn't pick, and that's one more thing to enjoy.
ENTJ>ENTJ.hidden: You're great at sticking to plans, and you can also enjoy the unplanned. Have you ever had plans rained out, just hung around at home, and found it surprisingly fun? Use it, and people around you will feel more relaxed with you.

ENTJ>ENTP.title: You keep changing how you do things, right on the spot.
ENTJ>ENTP.body: You always meet deadlines. But you think the way you get there can change depending on how you feel that day. Even on a trip, you only lock in the time to head home, and if a place catches your eye along the way, you stop by.
ENTJ>ENTP.say: "As long as it's done by Friday, do it however you like."
ENTJ>ENTP.do: When you think of a new way, you immediately ask everyone, "Want to try it?"
ENTJ>ENTP.worry: You want to stick to what you decided, and you want to try more interesting ways, both at once. When you keep changing how things are done, you worry you're jerking people around.
ENTJ>ENTP.karai: While helping a friend with a problem, you get more fired up than they are.
ENTJ>ENTP.aru: You planned the order of places for the trip, but when you arrive you think, "Actually, I'm curious about that shop," and change the plan yourself.
ENTJ>ENTP.why: By nature, you're the type who wants to make a plan and follow it properly. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to feel that plans are something you're allowed to change. Even so, the final time to head home still stays firmly in your head. As long as you make it home on time, you feel free to change anything in between, so you can change the plan yourself and go to a shop that caught your eye after you arrive.
ENTJ>ENTP.yure: The question that makes you waver is "Do you plan ahead or decide on the spot?" Picture a work deadline, and you lean toward planning. Picture a day off, and you lean toward the spot.
ENTJ>ENTP.yure_s: The question that makes you waver is "Do you plan ahead or decide on the spot?" Picture an assignment deadline, and you lean toward planning. Picture a day off, and you lean toward the spot.
ENTJ>ENTP.plus: You want to change plans because you notice more interesting ways. Someone who keeps the goal and changes the method is a big help when things keep changing.
ENTJ>ENTP.tip: When you go out with friends, say at the start, "Let's decide the afternoon when we get there." Then changing plans is part of the deal, and no one feels jerked around.
ENTJ>ENTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to work back from the goal and set the order. It shows when a deadline gets close and your head suddenly clears and you start lining up tasks. Use it earlier, and people at work will trust you as someone who always finishes.
ENTJ>ENTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to work back from the goal and set the order. It shows when a deadline gets close and your head suddenly clears and you start lining up tasks. Use it earlier, and people in class projects and group work will trust you as someone who always finishes.

ENTJ>INFJ.title: You quickly notice who might get left behind.
ENTJ>INFJ.body: When a younger coworker or teammate tells you about their future, you're already thinking through their plan in your head. In discussions you set the direction fast, but afterward you go over only to the people who didn't speak and ask, "What did you think?" You notice the people who might get left behind, too.
ENTJ>INFJ.say: "With this goal, I think everyone can keep going without pushing too hard."
ENTJ>INFJ.do: After a drama ends, you keep thinking about why the characters did what they did.
ENTJ>INFJ.worry: Even when you know the right direction, you can't say it if someone might get hurt. On days you've thought too much about others' feelings, you only feel like yourself again after time alone.
ENTJ>INFJ.karai: You say "Let's think about it later," but by bedtime you've already decided.
ENTJ>INFJ.aru: In the meeting you can quickly say, "Let's go this way," but the face of the person who barely spoke stays on your mind all the way home.
ENTJ>INFJ.aru_s: In a class discussion you can quickly say, "Let's go this way," but the face of the person who barely spoke stays on your mind all the way home.
ENTJ>INFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who leads in front of people and decides with logic. Through experience, you started paying attention to the feelings people are left with after a decision. You still decide quickly, and you think about feelings slowly afterward. During a discussion you put deciding first, so the feelings of people who couldn't speak up start quietly bothering you only once you're alone.
ENTJ>INFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself deciding as a leader or helping a friend with a problem.
ENTJ>INFJ.plus: You quickly notice people who might get left behind because you really look at each person. With you there, fewer people miss their chance to speak in discussions.
ENTJ>INFJ.tip: If someone's on your mind, ask everyone once at the end of the meeting: "Anyone else have thoughts?" You'll hear from them right there, so it won't follow you home as much.
ENTJ>INFJ.tip_s: If someone's on your mind, ask everyone once at the end of the discussion: "Anyone else have thoughts?" You'll hear from them right there, so it won't follow you home as much.
ENTJ>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to step up in front of people and move things along. It shows when a friend is stuck and you find yourself calling the shop for them and sorting it out. Use it, and you can show your kindness through action.

ENTJ>INFP.title: When you want to do something, you go all in.
ENTJ>INFP.body: Once you're serious, you can't stop: "We absolutely have to do this idea." But back home, you sometimes rethink things alone, wondering, "What did everyone actually think?" Some days you lead people, and some days you want to think about feelings by yourself.
ENTJ>INFP.say: "If I'm doing it, I want to do something I really believe in."
ENTJ>INFP.do: When you think of something you want to do, you picture it going well again and again.
ENTJ>INFP.worry: Wanting things to go well and wanting to do what you really want rarely line up. After a day of leading people, you want more alone time than you expect.
ENTJ>INFP.karai: The news gets you thinking ten years ahead, but you still haven't decided what's for dinner tonight.
ENTJ>INFP.aru: You got everyone excited with "Let's do this!", then on the way home you wonder, "Is this really what I want?"
ENTJ>INFP.why: By nature, you're the type who leads people, decides with logic, and follows the plan. As you've gotten older, you also came to want to check your own feelings alone before you act. In front of people, the drive you were born with comes out, and when you're alone, your current habit of valuing your feelings comes back. While you're getting everyone excited, you're running on momentum, and you only get to check your own feelings once you're alone on the way home.
ENTJ>INFP.yure: Three of your four tendencies differ, so your result can change a lot from test to test. Answer as the person out doing things with friends, or as the one listening to music alone at night, and you may get a completely different type.
ENTJ>INFP.plus: You stop to think because you want to stay honest with yourself. When you decide after thinking, you're less likely to have doubts later.
ENTJ>INFP.tip: Before starting something new, tell a friend you trust why you want to do it. Saying it out loud makes your reason clear, so it's easier to remember when you start to doubt.
ENTJ>INFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to see what you decide through to the end. It shows when, right before a move or a trip, you suddenly start knocking out tasks one by one. Use it on what you love, and your ideas take shape.
ENTJ>INFP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to see what you decide through to the end. It shows when, right before a test or a trip, you suddenly start knocking out tasks one by one. Use it on what you love, and your ideas take shape.

ENTJ>ENFJ.title: You keep things moving while checking in on everyone.
ENTJ>ENFJ.body: You can state the team's goal clearly. After the talk about the goal, you go over to anyone who got quiet and ask, "Was that hard to say earlier?" You keep an eye on both the numbers and people's faces.
ENTJ>ENFJ.say: "This is our goal for the month. Let's do it together!"
ENTJ>ENFJ.do: After a meeting, you ask someone who seems down, "You OK?"
ENTJ>ENFJ.do_s: After a team or club meeting, you ask someone who seems down, "You OK?"
ENTJ>ENFJ.worry: When you should be firm, you picture their face and end up too soft. Trying to move everyone forward, you're the one running around the most.
ENTJ>ENFJ.karai: When planning stalls in the group chat, you drop three possible dates, and when no one answers, you add a fourth.
ENTJ>ENFJ.aru: You'd decided to talk to a junior about a mistake, but when you see their face, you end up softening how you say it.
ENTJ>ENFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who decides with logic. Through experience, you learned that even when something is right, how it comes across depends on how you say it. You can decide ahead of time what to point out, but you decide how to say it after seeing the person. When you see their face, not wanting to bring them down comes first, so your words end up softer.
ENTJ>ENFJ.yure: The key question is "Logic or feelings?" Picture work where you deliver numbers, and you lean toward logic. Picture looking after a junior, and you lean toward feelings.
ENTJ>ENFJ.yure_s: The key question is "Logic or feelings?" Picture setting the practice plan to win games, and you lean toward logic. Picture looking after a younger teammate, and you lean toward feelings.
ENTJ>ENFJ.plus: You soften your words because you really think about how the other person feels. When someone like that points something out, people can take it to heart.
ENTJ>ENFJ.tip: When you correct someone, pair "this is what happened" with "next time, please do this." It won't sound like blame, and they'll know right away what to fix.
ENTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to separate feelings from facts. It shows when a friend asks for love advice and you're the calmest one saying, "That's on them, not you." Use it, and you'll be more than kind; you'll really help people move forward.

ENTJ>ENFP.title: You actually make your fun ideas happen.
ENTJ>ENFP.body: Even with a surprise you started on a whim, before you know it you've decided the flow of the day and the budget. You said "Let's keep it casual," but you're the first one writing out who's buying what and when. You can turn fun ideas into something real.
ENTJ>ENFP.say: "Anyone want to go to next month's festival? I'll get the tickets."
ENTJ>ENFP.do: Even with someone you just met, you quickly get excited talking about things you both love.
ENTJ>ENFP.worry: You want to keep starting fun things, but you also want to finish everything you start, so you get busy. With someone who just wants you to listen, you jump to the practical stuff first and regret it later.
ENTJ>ENFP.karai: The longest message in the group chat is usually from you.
ENTJ>ENFP.aru: You're the one who said, "Let's keep it casual," but somehow you're the most serious about setting times and roles.
ENTJ>ENFP.why: By nature, you're the type who decides with logic and keeps things on track. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value the fun of the moment and how everyone feels. You really mean it when you say "Let's keep it loose," and the hands that plan things out are the ones you were born with. The more you want everyone to have fun, the more you want to plan it out so the day goes well, and the person who suggested it ends up being the most serious one.
ENTJ>ENFP.yure: You tend to waver on "logic or feelings" and "plan or go with the moment." Your answers change depending on whether you picture yourself preparing an event or hanging out with friends.
ENTJ>ENFP.plus: You end up running things because you really want to make everyone's fun happen. Not many people can take an idea and actually do it.
ENTJ>ENFP.tip: At the next get-together, hand one whole job over to someone else. With less to run, you'll get to enjoy it too.
ENTJ>ENFP.hidden: When a friend is venting, do you ever find yourself thinking, "Maybe this is the cause"? That's your temperament's power to find causes with logic. Use it along with your kind listening, and people will rely on you even more for advice.

ENTJ>ISTJ.title: Even with big goals, you check the numbers first.
ENTJ>ISTJ.body: Right after you state a big goal, you start checking last month's numbers. The day after you say, "Next year I want to do this," you've made a spreadsheet of how far you can go with the money you have now. You can turn what you want to do into a real plan with numbers and steps.
ENTJ>ISTJ.body_s: Right after you state a big goal, you start checking last year's records. The day after you say, "I want to make it this far at the next meet," you've written down how much you need to improve from your current record. You can turn what you want to do into a real plan with numbers and steps.
ENTJ>ISTJ.say: "First, can I see last month's numbers?"
ENTJ>ISTJ.say_s: "First, can I see last year's records?"
ENTJ>ISTJ.do: Before shopping, you decide what to buy and how much to spend, and you don't go over.
ENTJ>ISTJ.worry: Between wanting to try something new and wanting a sure method, it takes you a while to decide. When you're the organizer for too long, you start missing quiet time to work.
ENTJ>ISTJ.karai: You arrive 10 minutes early and think the friend who shows up right on time is "late."
ENTJ>ISTJ.aru: The same night you think, "It'd be fun to open a shop like this," you're looking up rent on your phone and doing the math.
ENTJ>ISTJ.aru_s: The same night you think, "It'd be fun to run a booth like this at the school festival," you're looking up the cost of supplies on your phone and doing the math.
ENTJ>ISTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who pulls people in and pictures big things. Through experience, you settled into a way of checking ideas with numbers before acting. You still have the ability to picture things, and right after that, your checking hands get to work. The more interesting an idea seems, the sooner you want to know if it can really work, and you've started doing the money math that same night.
ENTJ>ISTJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Facts or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself pitching a new project or comparing data.
ENTJ>ISTJ.plus: Even if it takes time to get started, you're less likely to fail. You can turn big things into something truly doable with numbers and steps.
ENTJ>ISTJ.tip: Decide to start once you understand about 70 percent. The other 30 percent you can only learn by doing, so this keeps you from researching forever.
ENTJ>ISTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to get people involved and move things forward. It shows when, as soon as you're ready, you start calling everyone involved and end up as the organizer. Use it, and you can make your solid plans even bigger.

ENTJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who sees what they decided through to the end.
ENTJ>ISFJ.body: You see what you're asked to do all the way through. Even while you're organizing, if you notice "That person seems down today," you quietly check on them later. Your planner has everyone's important dates written in along with your to-dos.
ENTJ>ISFJ.say: "Are you feeling okay? Let's not push it — a little at a time."
ENTJ>ISFJ.do: Helping a friend move, you decide the order to carry things and tell everyone.
ENTJ>ISFJ.do_s: Helping set up for the school festival, you decide the order to carry things and tell everyone.
ENTJ>ISFJ.worry: Even when you want to take the lead, you step back out of care for others. The harder you try to do your part well, the more your own rest gets pushed back.
ENTJ>ISFJ.karai: You finished packing for the trip three days ago, so the night before there's nothing left to do.
ENTJ>ISFJ.aru: While making the team's plan for the year, you also put everyone's birthday on the calendar.
ENTJ>ISFJ.aru_s: While making the club's plan for the year, you also put every member's birthday on the calendar.
ENTJ>ISFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who stands in front of people, looks ahead, and decides with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value quietly supporting each person in front of you. Your planning skills are the same, but what you put into the plan has changed. When you make a plan, you care about everyone's important days as much as the tasks, so you even write birthdays on the calendar.
ENTJ>ISFJ.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself setting direction at work, or looking after family and friends, and you may get totally different types.
ENTJ>ISFJ.yure_s: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself setting direction in a club or student council, or looking after family and friends, and you may get totally different types.
ENTJ>ISFJ.plus: You remember birthdays because you care about each person. Not many people keep an eye on the future and on the people close to them.
ENTJ>ISFJ.tip: Put your own days off on the calendar first, just like work plans. When your rest days are set, they don't get pushed back.
ENTJ>ISFJ.tip_s: Put your own days off on the calendar first, just like assignments and club plans. When your rest days are set, they don't get pushed back.
ENTJ>ISFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to picture years ahead. It shows when you listen to a junior and think, "In three years, they'll be a leader." Tell them, and it will give them confidence.

ENTJ>ESTJ.title: You make the way things work at your job a little better, step by step.
ENTJ>ESTJ.title_s: You make the way your club does things a little better, step by step.
ENTJ>ESTJ.body: When you bring a new idea, you also bring three past examples that worked. Even when you think "We should change this," you first write down what's been working with the current way. Even when you change things, you watch where you're stepping.
ENTJ>ESTJ.say: "Okay, tomorrow we start with this one."
ENTJ>ESTJ.do: When a number at work bugs you, you go check it yourself before asking anyone.
ENTJ>ESTJ.do_s: When a club record bugs you, you go check it yourself before asking anyone.
ENTJ>ESTJ.worry: You want to change things, and you also want to protect what's working, so you're unsure how far to go. You tend to use yourself as the standard and expect others to move at your speed.
ENTJ>ESTJ.karai: Right after saying, "Do it however you like," you explain exactly how to do it.
ENTJ>ESTJ.aru: While talking about wanting to buy a house someday, you're also keeping close track of how much this month's electric bill went up.
ENTJ>ESTJ.aru_s: While talking about wanting to study abroad someday, you're also keeping close track of how much this month's phone bill went up.
ENTJ>ESTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and thinks about it. Through experience, you started looking at the current numbers first, especially when the plan is big. The part of you that pictures "someday" is still there. Because you truly want to make "someday" happen, you don't overlook the numbers right in front of you, like how much you spent this month.
ENTJ>ESTJ.yure: Questions about how you see things are where your answers split. Picture yourself planning a new project, and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself running daily work, and you lean toward facts.
ENTJ>ESTJ.yure_s: Questions about how you see things are where your answers split. Picture yourself thinking up a new idea, and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself keeping a club or class running, and you lean toward facts.
ENTJ>ESTJ.plus: Even when you think up new things, you keep a close eye on what's working at your job right now. That's why people feel safe following your decisions.
ENTJ>ESTJ.plus_s: Even when you think up new things, you're paying attention to how your team is really doing right now. That's why people feel safe following your decisions.
ENTJ>ESTJ.tip: When you suggest something new, say first, "Only this part changes; everything else stays the same." When people know what isn't changing, they'll listen with less worry.
ENTJ>ESTJ.hidden: While doing your usual work, do you ever think, "This could work for something else too"? That's your temperament's power to find what no one has noticed yet. When it happens, tell someone nearby right away, and it could start a new project.
ENTJ>ESTJ.hidden_s: While doing your usual practice or tasks, do you ever think, "This could work for something else too"? That's your temperament's power to find what no one has noticed yet. When it happens, tell someone nearby right away, and it could start a new idea.

ENTJ>ESFJ.title: You go around thanking everyone.
ENTJ>ESFJ.body: You prepare an event carefully, and on the day you go around saying "Thank you" to everyone. You're the first to notice a table running low on drinks and go get more. You care about both the results and everyone having a good time.
ENTJ>ESFJ.say: "Let's hear everyone out and decide today."
ENTJ>ESFJ.do: When meeting friends, you set the time to wrap up around everyone's trains home.
ENTJ>ESFJ.worry: Even when you want results, you don't want to upset anyone. You're so glad to be relied on that you take on too much, and suddenly your schedule is full.
ENTJ>ESFJ.karai: You plan everyone's seats and put yourself at the end, where it's easy to order.
ENTJ>ESFJ.aru: You prepared the event perfectly, but on the day you're so busy checking that everyone's having fun that you barely eat.
ENTJ>ESFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who pictures what's ahead and decides with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you started watching closely whether the people in front of you are enjoying themselves. Up to the prep, it's the planning skill you were born with, and on the day, your current attentiveness takes the lead. On the day, your head is full of watching how everyone is doing, so you end up putting off eating yourself.
ENTJ>ESFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "logic or feelings." The result depends on whether you answer picturing yourself setting direction in a meeting or planning a welcome party.
ENTJ>ESFJ.yure_s: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "logic or feelings." The result depends on whether you answer picturing yourself setting direction in a group discussion or planning a welcome party for new members.
ENTJ>ESFJ.plus: You care more about others than yourself because you really want everyone to enjoy themselves. Get-togethers with you there always feel good.
ENTJ>ESFJ.tip: On event days, decide that you'll sit and eat for the first 15 minutes. Everyone's busy eating at the start anyway, so looking after people can wait a bit.
ENTJ>ESFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to decide quickly with logic. It shows when a discussion drags on and you say, "OK, let's decide this much today." Use it along with your thoughtfulness, and you can take care of everyone's time too.

ENTJ>ISTP.title: You get it done with your hands before you talk about it.
ENTJ>ISTP.body: You don't say much, but before anyone notices, the work is already done. While the discussion keeps going, you quickly try things out on your own. Rather than talking it over, you start by working with your own hands.
ENTJ>ISTP.do: Once something's decided, you keep the explanation short and start your own work right away.
ENTJ>ISTP.worry: Sometimes you want to plan far ahead, sometimes you want to act on the spot, and the switching makes it hard to find your own pace. When you're put in charge, you start wanting time to work alone with your hands.
ENTJ>ISTP.karai: In long meetings, you think, "It'd be faster to just fix it quietly."
ENTJ>ISTP.karai_s: In long group discussions, you think, "It'd be faster to just fix it quietly."
ENTJ>ISTP.aru: When an appliance acts up, you start poking at it to fix it before reading the manual, and your family says, "Talk to us first."
ENTJ>ISTP.why: By nature, you're the type who leads people, thinks ahead, and follows the plan. As you've gotten older, you picked up a way of working alone with your hands, checking things by touching them. Your logical mind is the same, and the way you check things has shifted to using your hands. Your body has learned that touching something tells you faster than reading the manual, so your hands move before you even ask anyone.
ENTJ>ISTP.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Depending on whether you picture yourself talking about goals as a leader or working alone, your type can change quite a bit.
ENTJ>ISTP.plus: Your hands move before you explain because you need to check things for real. You can set the goal and finish it yourself, so your plans never stay just talk.
ENTJ>ISTP.tip: Before you start working on something, just say, "I'm going to do this now." It cuts down a lot on mix-ups with your family or team.
ENTJ>ISTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to organize people and plan ahead. It shows when, on a trip with friends, you find yourself sorting out the transfers and the budget. Use it at work, and you'll go from "skilled" to "someone we can leave it to."
ENTJ>ISTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to organize people and plan ahead. It shows when, on a trip with friends, you find yourself sorting out the transfers and the budget. Use it in clubs and group projects, and you'll go from "skilled" to "someone we can leave it to."

ENTJ>ISFP.title: When it matters, you decide firmly.
ENTJ>ISFP.body: Most of the time, you're smiling and listening. But at important moments, you decide so firmly that people are surprised. You usually go along with "Anything's fine," but when it's time to choose where to go on a trip, you research it yourself and pick the best place.
ENTJ>ISFP.say: "I really like this. I could look at it forever."
ENTJ>ISFP.do: For things in your room, you choose by whether they make you feel good, not by price.
ENTJ>ISFP.worry: You want things calm, but when things drag on, you're secretly annoyed. You hold in what you want to say, and later it can come out suddenly and too strongly.
ENTJ>ISFP.karai: You said "Anywhere is fine," but you know the most places to pick from.
ENTJ>ISFP.aru: You say, "Anywhere's fine," when picking a café, but you end up leading everyone to a quiet place with outlets.
ENTJ>ISFP.why: By nature, you're the type who leads people, thinks ahead, decides with logic, and follows the plan. Through experience, you came to value time alone and how you feel in the moment. Day to day, your current gentleness shows, and at important moments, the deciding ability you were born with comes out. You mean it when you say "Anywhere is fine," but your mind is quietly weighing things like noise level and outlets, so before you know it, you're leading everyone to a place that fits.
ENTJ>ISFP.yure: All four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself carrying responsibility at work, or on a day off surrounded by things you love, and you may get opposite types.
ENTJ>ISFP.yure_s: All four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself pulling everyone together in a club or class, or on a day off surrounded by things you love, and you may get opposite types.
ENTJ>ISFP.plus: You're gentle but have things you won't give up, because you know what matters to you. That's why you can decide without doubt when it counts.
ENTJ>ISFP.tip: When you do have a preference, add one line: "Anywhere's fine, but somewhere quiet would be nice." That alone makes it easier for others to choose.
ENTJ>ISFP.hidden: When you go shopping with a friend, do you ever casually say, "This one will last longer"? That's your temperament's power to judge things with logic. Use it when you're going along with others, and your words will carry more weight.

ENTJ>ESTP.title: When it counts, you decide in a flash.
ENTJ>ESTP.body: You plan your strategy carefully, but when it's go time, your body moves before you think. Even with notes you prepared, you watch how people react and switch the order of what you say on the spot. That's why you're strong when it really counts.
ENTJ>ESTP.say: "We can talk later! Let's grab the seats first."
ENTJ>ESTP.do: When a friend can't decide what to buy, you're quick to say, "This one's the better deal."
ENTJ>ESTP.worry: Even when you want to plan ahead, you jump at whatever's fun in front of you, and the plan gets pushed back. You skip checks to move fast, and sometimes regret it later.
ENTJ>ESTP.karai: When a friend vents, you say "OK, here's what to do" before "I get it."
ENTJ>ESTP.aru: You prepared your presentation carefully, but when you see their faces, you change the order right on the spot.
ENTJ>ESTP.aru_s: You prepared your group presentation carefully, but when you see the audience's faces, you change the order right on the spot.
ENTJ>ESTP.why: By nature, you're the type who looks ahead and makes plans. Through all kinds of experiences, you also learned to read people and act on the spot. Your preparation is the way you were born with, and how you move in the moment is what you learned through experience. Because your prep is solid, you have room to change the order based on the other person's face when it's time to deliver.
ENTJ>ESTP.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "plan or the moment." The result depends on whether you answer picturing yourself taking time to prepare or deciding quickly on site.
ENTJ>ESTP.plus: You can change your approach on the spot because you watch people's reactions closely. You've prepared, so even when you change things, the plan doesn't fall apart.
ENTJ>ESTP.tip: When you prepare, pick one thing you'll make sure to say. Keep that one thing, and you can change the rest on the spot without losing your point.
ENTJ>ESTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to read where things are heading years ahead. It shows when you see the news and just know, "This is going to be big next year." Trust that hunch and move a little early, and you can stay a step ahead at work too.
ENTJ>ESTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to read where things are heading years ahead. It shows when you see the news and just know, "This is going to be big next year." Trust that hunch and move a little early, and you can stay a step ahead in school and in your club too.

ENTJ>ESFP.title: You get everyone excited and lead them right along.
ENTJ>ESFP.body: At the after-party, you're the one getting everyone hyped, while quietly starting to talk about the next goal. While everyone is laughing, you've already picked the date for the next get-together. You can move everyone forward while keeping the fun going.
ENTJ>ESFP.do: At parties, you talk to people who are new so they can join the conversation.
ENTJ>ESFP.do_s: At class get-togethers, you talk to people who are new so they can join the conversation.
ENTJ>ESFP.worry: Even when you want to enjoy the moment, part of your mind is always on the next thing to prepare. Because you care about everyone's feelings, you tend to dwell on it after saying something tough.
ENTJ>ESFP.karai: With an empty weekend coming, by Friday night you've texted someone, "Free tomorrow?"
ENTJ>ESFP.aru: It was a trip you decided on a whim, but somehow you're the one carefully booking the hotel and the train times.
ENTJ>ESFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks ahead, decides with logic, and follows the plan. Through experience, you came to value the fun in front of you and how everyone feels, and to act in the moment. What gets you to suggest things is your current mood, and what gets things decided is the planning skill you were born with. Even on a trip decided on a whim, you want to make sure nobody has trouble on the day, so the hotel and train times are what you pin down most carefully.
ENTJ>ESFP.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as the person in charge of a team, or as someone having fun with friends, and you may get completely different types.
ENTJ>ESFP.plus: Even things decided on a whim, you see all the way through. You get things going and also pull them together, so people around you can relax and have fun.
ENTJ>ESFP.tip: Don't carry all the prep alone; split jobs like "hype person" and "cleanup" with someone. That way you get time to enjoy yourself too.
ENTJ>ESFP.hidden: While listening to a friend, do ideas pop up like, "That could be even more fun if..."? That's your temperament's power to picture what's ahead. Use it at work too, and you'll go from the fun one to the one trusted with planning.
ENTJ>ESFP.hidden_s: While listening to a friend, do ideas pop up like, "That could be even more fun if..."? That's your temperament's power to picture what's ahead. Use it in your club or the school festival too, and you'll go from the fun one to the one trusted with planning.

ENTP>INTJ.title: You think your ideas through, on your own.
ENTP>INTJ.body: You take ideas that come up in casual talk, think them through alone, and turn them into a plan. When you and a friend say, "Wouldn't it be cool if this existed?", you go home, write out the steps, and even decide where to start. You don't leave ideas just sitting there.
ENTP>INTJ.say: "Wouldn't it be interesting to think about it backwards?"
ENTP>INTJ.do: When you see a new product everyone's talking about, you look up how it works before buying.
ENTP>INTJ.worry: Even when you want to build ideas by talking, too much talking tires you out and you want to be alone. Between wanting to try right away and wanting to plan first, you often start late.
ENTP>INTJ.karai: You pick up one book at a bookstore, and that night you stay up late watching related videos.
ENTP>INTJ.aru: The next day, you're explaining how to actually do something you thought up while chatting with a friend. Your friend says, "Wait, you were serious?"
ENTP>INTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who expands ideas while talking with people and acts on the spot. Through all kinds of experiences, you started thinking things through alone and planning far ahead. Ideas come to you while you're talking with people, and you shape them when you're alone. Even if it was a light idea in casual talk, once you're home alone you can't stop thinking about how to make it happen, so by the next day you can already explain how to do it.
ENTP>INTJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Planner or go-with-the-moment?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself tossing out ideas while chatting or looking things up alone.
ENTP>INTJ.plus: You can turn ideas into something real fast because you can see how to do it in your head. Seeing your ideas all the way through is one of your good points.
ENTP>INTJ.tip: When you have an idea, tell just one person, "I'm thinking about this," before you work it out in detail. You'll get feedback early, and it'll turn out even better.
ENTP>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to build ideas while talking with people. It shows when a casual chat turns into an exciting new plan with someone. When you get stuck, try talking with someone first.

ENTP>INTP.title: Even mid-talk, you suddenly want to think alone.
ENTP>INTP.body: One minute you're leaning in saying, "Tell me more!", and the next you suddenly want to think alone. You look up the rest of an exciting conversation by yourself at home, and a few days later you come back and say, "Hey, turns out it was like this."
ENTP>INTP.say: "Give me a sec to think about this on my own."
ENTP>INTP.do: When something catches your interest, you spend your whole day off looking into it.
ENTP>INTP.worry: There's a big gap between days you want to talk and days you don't want to see anyone, so planning is hard. Thinking is so fun that sometimes you feel satisfied before actually doing anything.
ENTP>INTP.karai: On days with no one to talk to, you argue with online articles in your head.
ENTP>INTP.aru: When a conversation with friends gets going, you're the most into it, but the moment you get home, you don't want to talk to anyone.
ENTP>INTP.why: By nature, you're the type who gets energy from talking with people. As you've gotten older, you came to recharge by resting alone. When the conversation is interesting, you step forward like you were born to, but the way you recharge is your current way. You use up a lot of energy while things are lively, so by the time you get home, you want to be quiet by yourself and recharge.
ENTP>INTP.yure: Your answers split on "Do people give you energy, or do you need time alone?" Depending on whether you picture a night of deep talk with friends or time alone at home looking things up, you may go back and forth between two types.
ENTP>INTP.plus: You go quiet at home because you're thinking over what you talked about. That's why your thoughts go deep.
ENTP>INTP.tip: On weekends, make plans for only one of the two days. Knowing you can rest the next day lets you enjoy the day you're invited out all the way through.
ENTP>INTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to quickly warm up to people you've just met. It shows when, at a gathering full of strangers, you find yourself asking questions and keeping the conversation going. Use it, and you'll make more new connections at work too.
ENTP>INTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to quickly warm up to people you've just met. It shows when, at a gathering full of strangers, you find yourself asking questions and keeping the conversation going. Use it, and you'll make more new connections at school and at your part-time job too.

ENTP>ENTJ.title: When you get an idea, you set the plan that same day.
ENTP>ENTJ.body: Just when you've pitched a fun idea in a meeting, you've already decided who does what and the deadline. The moment you say, "I want to try this," you start writing the schedule on the whiteboard. You turn ideas into plans right away.
ENTP>ENTJ.body_s: Just when you've pitched a fun idea in a group discussion, you've already decided who does what and the deadline. The moment you say, "I want to try this," you start writing the schedule on the board. You turn ideas into plans right away.
ENTP>ENTJ.say: "How about this? Let's try it once by next week."
ENTP>ENTJ.do: You started working out on a whim, but by week two you're tracking reps and weight in an app.
ENTP>ENTJ.worry: Wanting to try new ideas clashes with wanting to stick to the plan, and sometimes you get trapped by your own rules. You move so fast that you're slow to notice people who can't keep up.
ENTP>ENTJ.karai: The hobby you "just sort of started" has somehow become the most serious one.
ENTP>ENTJ.aru: You just said, "Let's take a trip!" on a whim, and the next day you've set the dates and budget and posted them in the group chat.
ENTP>ENTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who wants to go with the flow of the moment. Through experience, you learned that ideas don't move forward unless you set a date. You're still quick on your feet with ideas, and now you're also quick to decide. You don't want what you said to stay just talk, so even for a spur-of-the-moment trip, by the next day you've picked the dates and the budget and sent them out.
ENTP>ENTJ.yure: Your answers wobble on "Do you like to plan or go with the moment?" Picture yourself running a project at work, and you lean toward planning. Picture a carefree day off, and you lean toward the moment.
ENTP>ENTJ.yure_s: Your answers wobble on "Do you like to plan or go with the moment?" Picture yourself running the prep for the school festival, and you lean toward planning. Picture a carefree day off, and you lean toward the moment.
ENTP>ENTJ.plus: You can make ideas happen fast because you can think up fun things and also see them through. When something new is starting, people really count on you.
ENTP>ENTJ.tip: Leave some "no plans" time once a week. If you have separate time to try out ideas, you won't have to break the plans you've made.
ENTP>ENTJ.hidden: On a day the trains stop and your plans fall apart, do you somehow get excited and start looking for another route? That's your temperament's power to enjoy the unplanned. Use it, and people will count on you most when things go wrong.

ENTP>ENTP.title: You're always looking for something interesting.
ENTP>ENTP.body: Has "But what if we just dropped all of that?" become something you say all the time? Even when a plan is almost settled, you bring up another idea, "But we could also do this," and open the conversation up again. When a topic has no single answer, you get totally absorbed. In places with only routine tasks, you tend to lose energy.
ENTP>ENTP.say: "Who decided it had to be this way, anyway?"
ENTP>ENTP.do: When a new shop opens, you go right away and tell friends how it's different from the others.
ENTP>ENTP.worry: You're good at starting, but you tend to blame yourself for getting bored with keeping things up. When routine tasks keep going, you slowly lose your motivation.
ENTP>ENTP.karai: Once a debate heats up, you forget you started on the other side.
ENTP>ENTP.aru: You were supposed to be picking a place for dinner with friends. Somehow you got into a big talk about what makes a good restaurant, and you still haven't picked one.
ENTP>ENTP.why: Both what you were born with and what you learned through experience are about expanding ideas while talking with people. Through all kinds of experiences, you've seen many times how something interesting turns up once a conversation grows. Because of that, your attention tends to go to thinking rather than deciding. A question like "What makes a restaurant good?" feels more interesting than the task of picking a restaurant, so the conversation spreads in that direction.
ENTP>ENTP.yure: Your results tend to stay steady, with the same type coming up again and again. If a different one appears, you may be in a stretch of adapting to a strict role, or low on energy from too little new stimulation.
ENTP>ENTP.plus: Your hobbies change often not because you get bored easily, but because you're quick to find interesting things. All the things you've tried will come in handy in unexpected places.
ENTP>ENTP.tip: For a new hobby, decide on "a one-month trial" before buying gear. If you only buy for the ones that stick, your room and wallet stay neat.
ENTP>ENTP.hidden: You act on ideas, and you also have the power to keep at one thing steadily. It shows when you make a favorite dish again and again, slowly making it your own. Use it at work too, and people will feel safe leaving things to you.
ENTP>ENTP.hidden_s: You act on ideas, and you also have the power to keep at one thing steadily. It shows when you make a favorite dish again and again, slowly making it your own. Use it in your club or your studies too, and people will feel safe leaving things to you.

ENTP>INFJ.title: When you listen, you pick up on what people really feel.
ENTP>INFJ.body: When you listen to a friend's worries, you start to see feelings they haven't noticed themselves. After listening, you think it over alone at home, and the next time you meet, you choose your words and say, "About what you told me the other day..." When you listen, you pay close attention to the feelings behind the words.
ENTP>INFJ.do: You watch favorite movies many times, finding a new way to see them each time.
ENTP>INFJ.worry: Even when you think of something interesting, you hesitate to say it in case it hurts someone. You take in people's feelings so fully that you need plenty of time alone to rest.
ENTP>INFJ.karai: Just talking about a trip, you're already imagining daily life in a town you've never been to.
ENTP>INFJ.aru: While listening to a friend's worries, you said, "Isn't this what you really want?" and they said, "How did you know?"
ENTP>INFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who expands ideas by talking with people and thinks with logic. Through experience, you started thinking things through alone and picking up on how others feel. Your ability to follow the logic of a story is the same, and now you also have an eye for feelings. When you follow both the logic of what someone says and their feelings, you start to see the "what I really want" they haven't put into words.
ENTP>INFJ.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Picture yourself chatting loudly with friends, or quietly helping a friend with a problem, and you may get totally different types.
ENTP>INFJ.plus: You notice people's true feelings because you really listen. Someone who notices feelings that are hard to put into words is precious to the people around them.
ENTP>INFJ.tip: On days you help someone with a problem, take a little time for yourself, like buying your favorite drink on the way home. If you rest up, you'll be glad to listen next time too.
ENTP>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to brighten a room by talking. It shows when, at a get-together after a long time, you find yourself joking and keeping things going. Try starting a conversation yourself once in a while, and you'll have more friends you can talk with.

ENTP>INFP.title: You love to daydream, and you're kind.
ENTP>INFP.body: On nights you got caught up talking with everyone, you're at home alone letting your imagination run. Even with a funny idea, you think once, "Will this make anyone feel bad?", before you say it. Even when you're talking about things you love, you're watching the faces of the people listening.
ENTP>INFP.do: You and a friend trade silly ideas and get carried away with made-up stories until midnight.
ENTP>INFP.worry: Even if logic says yes, you can't move unless your heart agrees. After a fun time, you find yourself alone, wondering if anything you said hurt someone.
ENTP>INFP.karai: At the bookstore, you find a book on a shelf that has nothing to do with what you came for, and that's what you buy.
ENTP>INFP.aru: Lying in bed, you remember a joke you made while everyone was having fun and wonder, "Did that hurt anyone?"
ENTP>INFP.why: By nature, you're the type who talks with people and thinks with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value time to think alone and other people's feelings. Around people, conversation flows the way you were born with, and when you're alone, your current consideration comes back. While you're talking, you're absorbed in the fun, but once it's quiet you start wondering how the other person took it, so you end up replaying your jokes in bed.
ENTP>INFP.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself having fun with friends or daydreaming alone.
ENTP>INFP.plus: You replay your words because you don't want to hurt people as much as you want to make them laugh. That's why few people get hurt by your jokes.
ENTP>INFP.tip: If something you said is bugging you, just ask lightly next time: "About the other day, you're not bothered, right?" Most people don't even remember, so you'll spend less time worrying alone at night.
ENTP>INFP.hidden: Watching a drama, do you ever notice, "Wait, this part doesn't make sense"? That's your temperament's power to quickly spot things that don't add up. Use it at work, and you'll be someone who finds problems early.
ENTP>INFP.hidden_s: Watching a drama, do you ever notice, "Wait, this part doesn't make sense"? That's your temperament's power to quickly spot things that don't add up. Use it on assignments and group projects, and you'll be someone who finds problems early.

ENTP>ENFJ.title: You speak up so no one gets left behind.
ENTP>ENFJ.body: You can talk about new ideas in a fun way. When someone is about to get left behind, you notice right away and check in with them. Before a discussion, you even think about what people who might disagree would say, and prepare your answers.
ENTP>ENFJ.say: "Want to figure out together how to make everyone excited about it?"
ENTP>ENFJ.do: When planning an outing, you quietly pick a place where even the friend who isn't sporty can have fun.
ENTP>ENFJ.worry: Even when you want to say something sharp, you sometimes hold back, thinking about the mood and people's feelings. The more you organize, the less time you have to freely try your ideas.
ENTP>ENFJ.karai: It was just a chat, but now you're pulling everyone in: "Let's actually do this!"
ENTP>ENFJ.aru: When you think of something fun, before telling everyone, you go talk one by one to the people who might say no.
ENTP>ENFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks with logic and acts on the spot. Through experience, you came to value people's feelings and prepare ahead of time. You still enjoy coming up with ideas, and the way you present them has changed. You know that even a good idea leaves some people's feelings behind if you spring it on them, so you go and hear each person out first.
ENTP>ENFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "logic or feelings" and "plan or the moment." The result depends on whether you picture yourself tossing out ideas or bringing everyone together.
ENTP>ENFJ.plus: You go talk to people first because you don't want to leave anyone behind. Not many people can liven things up and look out for everyone too.
ENTP>ENFJ.tip: On days you're the organizer, decide one part of your idea you want to keep before you start. You won't end up giving everything away, so you won't feel uneasy afterward.
ENTP>ENFJ.hidden: Have you ever had a prepared story fall flat, then saved the moment with something else on the spot? That's your temperament's power to change the flow on the spot. Use it, and you can enjoy days that don't go as planned.

ENTP>ENFP.title: You think things are more fun when everyone does them together.
ENTP>ENFP.body: When you talk, people somehow gather around. As you share one idea after another, you turn to quiet people and ask, "What do you think?" You enjoy the conversation while making sure nobody gets left out.
ENTP>ENFP.say: "Love it! Let's all try it next time!"
ENTP>ENFP.do: At family gatherings, you tweak the card game rules so even the little kids can win.
ENTP>ENFP.worry: Even when you want to say clearly what you think is right, you picture their disappointed face and stop. Your interests keep moving, and you also want to make time for people, so there's never enough time.
ENTP>ENFP.karai: Five minutes after saying, "Let's think calmly," you're the most excited one.
ENTP>ENFP.aru: You start to say, "Isn't that a little off?" to a friend, then see their face and add, "But I get how you feel."
ENTP>ENFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value wanting to make the other person smile. Your eye for spotting what doesn't add up is the same, and now you also care about choosing your words. Even when you notice something doesn't add up, seeing the other person's face makes you want to acknowledge their feelings first, so you add, "But I get how you feel."
ENTP>ENFP.yure: The question to watch is "Logic or feelings?" Picture yourself poking fun at a friend's story, and you lean toward logic. Picture yourself cheering up a friend, and you lean toward feelings.
ENTP>ENFP.plus: You soften your words because you care more about the relationship than about being right. People like that naturally end up with more friends they can be honest with.
ENTP>ENFP.tip: When you give your opinion, try saying "I get how you feel" first, then "and also..." What you say stays the same, but it lands differently.
ENTP>ENFP.hidden: Before a big purchase, do you compare reviews and prices across several sites? That's your temperament's power to calmly compare and choose. Use it at work, and you'll go from the fun one to someone people trust with decisions.
ENTP>ENFP.hidden_s: Before a big purchase, do you compare reviews and prices across several sites? That's your temperament's power to calmly compare and choose. Use it when your group has to decide something, and you'll go from the fun one to someone people trust with decisions.

ENTP>ISTJ.title: You try out a new way first, then tell people about it.
ENTP>ISTJ.body: Even when you think of a new way to do something, you try it small first and check the results with numbers. If you think "This might be faster," you compare the time with your usual way before choosing the better one. You don't let ideas stay just talk.
ENTP>ISTJ.say: "Sounds interesting. But let me check how we did it before."
ENTP>ISTJ.do: When an appliance breaks, you look into the cause yourself before sending it for repair.
ENTP>ISTJ.do_s: When your earbuds break, you look into the cause yourself before sending them for repair.
ENTP>ISTJ.worry: You want to try new things, and you want to stick with what's sure, so you can't settle. When you're stuck enforcing rules for a while, you miss having a place to share ideas.
ENTP>ISTJ.karai: Asked "How does this look?", you honestly point out what doesn't work, then regret it a little later.
ENTP>ISTJ.aru: Even when you think of a new way, you can't tell anyone until you've looked up lots of reviews and examples online.
ENTP>ISTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who talks with people about what could be and acts on the spot. As you've gotten older, you started checking past examples alone before moving forward. Your ability to come up with ideas is the same, and now there's an extra step of checking. You don't like talking up an idea and being wrong, so you can't tell anyone until you've checked reviews and examples.
ENTP>ISTJ.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself checking set procedures at work, or tossing out ideas while chatting with friends, and you may get nearly opposite types.
ENTP>ISTJ.yure_s: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself checking set routines in your club or class duties, or tossing out ideas while chatting with friends, and you may get nearly opposite types.
ENTP>ISTJ.plus: You don't speak up right away because you want your ideas to be truly useful. New ideas that have been checked carefully get accepted more easily and last longer.
ENTP>ISTJ.tip: Give yourself three days to research, and on day four, tell someone. Getting other people's opinions gets you to an answer faster than researching alone.
ENTP>ISTJ.hidden: During a break, do ideas ever start pouring out while you're just chatting? That's your temperament's power to build ideas by talking with people. Spend a little more time talking, and you'll find new tricks for your everyday work too.
ENTP>ISTJ.hidden_s: Between classes, do ideas ever start pouring out while you're just chatting? That's your temperament's power to build ideas by talking with people. Spend a little more time talking, and you'll find new tricks for your everyday studies and club too.

ENTP>ISFJ.title: You're kind, and you actually have lots of ideas.
ENTP>ISFJ.body: You finish the tasks you're given properly, and you've already figured out how to make it easier next time. While following the usual steps, you quietly swap the order to test, "This might be faster." You have both a side that looks out for people and a side that comes up with new ways of doing things.
ENTP>ISFJ.say: "I'll do the dishes. You sit down."
ENTP>ISFJ.do: Without telling anyone, you rearrange the shelf that's hard to use.
ENTP>ISFJ.worry: You're good at going along with others, but when the same thing keeps repeating, you slowly get tired of it. Even with a good idea, you sometimes hold it back because of the mood in the room.
ENTP>ISFJ.karai: "Just one more video," you say, and suddenly an hour's gone.
ENTP>ISFJ.aru: You say, "The usual way is fine," while thinking of ways to make the chores easier.
ENTP>ISFJ.aru_s: You say, "The usual way is fine," while thinking of ways to make classroom cleanup easier.
ENTP>ISFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who talks with people, thinks of new things, and wants to try them on the spot. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to quietly help the people around you and do what's been decided properly. What comes out of your mouth is your current carefulness, and in your head, the "Is there a better way?" you were born with keeps running. Even while you're saying "The usual way is fine," you can't stop thinking of an easier way in your head.
ENTP>ISFJ.yure: With all four tendencies different, your result can change a lot. Picture yourself supporting people at home or work, or following your curiosity to try something new, and your type can flip completely.
ENTP>ISFJ.yure_s: With all four tendencies different, your result can change a lot. Picture yourself supporting people at home or in class, or following your curiosity to try something new, and your type can flip completely.
ENTP>ISFJ.plus: The ideas you haven't voiced come from watching the people around you closely. Try sharing them little by little, and your family and coworkers will be glad you did.
ENTP>ISFJ.tip: Instead of "let's change everything," narrow it down to one: "Want to try just this part?" The smaller the suggestion, the more easily it gets accepted.
ENTP>ISFJ.hidden: When two friends argue, have you ever neatly sorted out both sides and said "So this is where you two don't line up"? That's your born ability to organize things with logic. Use it, and you'll become the person everyone turns to for advice.

ENTP>ESTJ.title: You suggest a new way and see it through.
ENTP>ESTJ.body: You bring up an idea and then carry it forward yourself. Once you say, "Let's try this," you assign roles that same day and tell everyone when it'll end. What you start, you finish on time.
ENTP>ESTJ.say: "Want to try doing it differently? I think it'd be faster."
ENTP>ESTJ.do: At the neighborhood festival, you suggest a new event and then set the roles and schedule for the day yourself.
ENTP>ESTJ.do_s: At the school festival, you suggest a new event and then set the roles and schedule for the day yourself.
ENTP>ESTJ.worry: You want to keep the rules, but you also want to try new things, so you're unsure how much to change. When you're in charge, you put being right first, and your words can come out harsh.
ENTP>ESTJ.karai: When no one speaks up in a meeting, you can't help saying, "OK, I'll start."
ENTP>ESTJ.karai_s: When no one speaks up in a group discussion, you can't help saying, "OK, I'll start."
ENTP>ESTJ.aru: You surprise everyone by saying, "Let's do today's meeting standing up." And you still finish right on time.
ENTP>ESTJ.aru_s: You surprise everyone by saying, "Let's do today's club meeting standing up." And you still finish right on time.
ENTP>ESTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks of new things and acts on the spot. Through experience, you came to value finishing on schedule. Your urge to try changing things is the same, and now you also have the ability to keep to the end time. Even when you change how things are done, people feel safe following you as long as you keep to the end time, so even an unusual meeting finishes right on schedule.
ENTP>ESTJ.why_s: By nature, you're the type who thinks of new things and acts on the spot. Through school life, you came to value finishing on schedule. Your urge to try changing things is the same, and now you also have the ability to keep to the end time. Even when you change how things are done, your club members feel safe following you as long as you keep to the end time, so even an unusual club meeting finishes right on schedule.
ENTP>ESTJ.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "plan or the moment." Your type can change depending on whether you answer as the person in charge at work or as someone acting on whims on a day off.
ENTP>ESTJ.yure_s: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "plan or the moment." Your type can change depending on whether you answer as the person keeping your club or class together or as someone acting on whims on a day off.
ENTP>ESTJ.plus: Not many people can change things on a whim and still finish on time. You can really change your workplace.
ENTP>ESTJ.plus_s: Not many people can change things on a whim and still finish on time. You can really change your club or class.
ENTP>ESTJ.tip: On days you're in charge, ask "What do you think?" once before giving instructions. Your point stays the same, but it sounds much less harsh.
ENTP>ESTJ.hidden: In the shower or on a walk, does a new way of doing your work ever just pop into your head? That's your temperament's power to come up with ideas that don't exist yet. Try them one at a time, and your workplace will get more interesting.
ENTP>ESTJ.hidden_s: In the shower or on a walk, does a new way of running your club or committee ever just pop into your head? That's your temperament's power to come up with ideas that don't exist yet. Try them one at a time, and your club or committee will get more interesting.

ENTP>ESFJ.title: You make the usual get-togethers more fun.
ENTP>ESFJ.body: You bring small new games to the usual get-togethers. You also take care of attendance and collecting money properly. Even on days you suggested the game, you don't forget to send photos to the people who couldn't come.
ENTP>ESFJ.say: "Wouldn't it be fun if we did this?"
ENTP>ESFJ.do: At work, you're the one saying, "Let's all go out for lunch today."
ENTP>ESFJ.do_s: At lunch, you're the one saying, "Let's all eat outside today."
ENTP>ESFJ.worry: Even when a slightly mean joke comes to mind, you keep it to yourself out of care for the other person. You love doing things for everyone, so you rarely get time to try your own ideas.
ENTP>ESFJ.karai: After a few days off alone, you start getting restless to talk to someone.
ENTP>ESFJ.aru: You're the one who suggested the silliest game at the get-together, and you're also the one who stays until the end to clean up.
ENTP>ESFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks of new things, thinks with logic, and acts on the spot. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to value the feelings of the people close to you and see things through to the end. You still enjoy suggesting things, and now you also feel responsible for how things end. Because it was a game you suggested, you want everyone's day to end on a good note, so you stay until the cleanup is done.
ENTP>ESFJ.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself running a get-together, or starting a game on a whim, and you may get a different type.
ENTP>ESFJ.plus: People really do notice how you work for everyone. People naturally gather around someone who's both fun and easy to be with.
ENTP>ESFJ.tip: Ask someone to help with even one part of the cleanup. That way you can enjoy the next game even more.
ENTP>ESFJ.hidden: When you hear the rules of a game, do you immediately see how to win? That's your temperament's power to build things with logic. Use it at work too, and your suggestions will make clear sense.
ENTP>ESFJ.hidden_s: When you hear the rules of a game, do you immediately see how to win? That's your temperament's power to build things with logic. Use it in group discussions and assignments too, and your suggestions will make clear sense.

ENTP>ISTP.title: When there's a problem, you quickly sort it out.
ENTP>ISTP.body: When a problem comes up, you start by touching it and checking it yourself. When a discussion drags on, you try things one by one in the meantime and show everyone first, "This works." When people are stuck, you quickly lend a hand.
ENTP>ISTP.say: "The manual can wait. Let's turn it on first."
ENTP>ISTP.do: When your bike chain comes off, you fix it right there.
ENTP>ISTP.worry: There's a big gap between wanting to talk and wanting to work without talking to anyone, so people may think you're moody. You also get torn between wanting to spread ideas and wanting to deal only with what's certain in front of you.
ENTP>ISTP.karai: When a friend asks how to use something, you skip the explanation and just do it for them.
ENTP>ISTP.aru: At a friend's house, a sticky drawer bugs you, and while listening to them you end up fixing it.
ENTP>ISTP.why: By nature, you're the type who expands ideas while talking with people. As you've gotten older, you started checking what's in front of you with your hands, alone. Your mind that thinks about how to make things better is the same, and now it goes straight to your hands. With a drawer that won't close right, you can tell where it's catching just by looking, so your hands move first even while you're listening to someone.
ENTP>ISTP.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Facts or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself sharing ideas with friends or fixing something alone.
ENTP>ISTP.plus: Your hands move while you listen because you're quick at thinking and doing. Being able to sort out problems quickly is a good thing about you.
ENTP>ISTP.tip: When you fix something for someone, add one line like, "This part was loose." They'll feel reassured, and they'll know what you did.
ENTP>ISTP.hidden: Looking at products in a shop, do you ever think, "Something like this would sell"? That's your temperament's power to picture things that don't exist yet. Tell people your ideas, and it might lead to new work.
ENTP>ISTP.hidden_s: Looking at products in a shop, do you ever think, "Something like this would sell"? That's your temperament's power to picture things that don't exist yet. Tell people your ideas, and it might lead to something new you start.

ENTP>ISFP.title: You find your own favorite places.
ENTP>ISFP.body: You take ideas that came up chatting with friends and try making them alone at home. On days off with no plans, you walk down streets that catch your interest and wander into small shops you find. When you find something you like, you look at it for a while.
ENTP>ISFP.say: "I want to look at this view a little longer."
ENTP>ISFP.do: An old sign you spot on a walk catches your eye, and you take photos of it from every angle.
ENTP>ISFP.worry: Even when you want to say something sharp, you hesitate when you think about the other person's feelings. You like having fun with people, but without time alone you tire quickly.
ENTP>ISFP.karai: You say you like to keep your schedule open, but you've already looked up every exhibit you're curious about.
ENTP>ISFP.aru: On a day off with no plans, you wander into a small shop by chance, love it, and by the time you leave you're already thinking about when to come back.
ENTP>ISFP.why: By nature, you're the type who talks with people and thinks about new things with logic. Through experience, you came to enjoy scenery and textures alone and to value your own feelings. You still move however ideas take you, and the way you enjoy things has become quieter. Even at a shop you walked into by chance, once your feelings decide "I like this place," you're already thinking about when you can come back.
ENTP>ISFP.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself deep in a lively talk with friends, or quietly taking in a view alone, and you may get a completely different type.
ENTP>ISFP.plus: You can get absorbed in fun things around you because you notice interesting things quickly. Thanks to that, your days are a little more fun.
ENTP>ISFP.tip: When you find a place you love, bring one friend next time. Sharing what you love with someone makes it even more fun.
ENTP>ISFP.hidden: When your favorite show comes up, do you find yourself talking with your hands? That's your temperament's power to get people excited by talking. Use it, and the things you love will reach the people around you too.

ENTP>ESTP.title: When an idea hits, you're on the move right away.
ENTP>ESTP.body: The same week you say, "This could be a business," you're already looking up prices. When a new shop catches your interest, you invite a friend and go before even reading reviews. You're quick to think and quick to act.
ENTP>ESTP.say: "Okay, let's go check it out right now!"
ENTP>ESTP.do: When you're unsure, you just go and see it with your own eyes.
ENTP>ESTP.worry: You want to chase both future possibilities and fun right now, so your schedule is always packed. Because you think while moving, you often move on before looking back and repeat the same mistakes.
ENTP>ESTP.karai: After the party, before anyone says, "What next?", you're already walking to the second spot.
ENTP>ESTP.karai_s: After eating out with everyone, before anyone says, "What next?", you're already walking to karaoke.
ENTP>ESTP.aru: The moment you think, "I want to go there," you message a friend, and that weekend you're both in line outside the shop.
ENTP>ESTP.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and thinks about it. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to feel that going and checking is faster than imagining. Getting energy from doing things with people and being able to act right away are things you've always had. The wish to go, someone to invite, and the speed to act all line up for you, so within the same week you thought of it, you're already standing in line at the shop.
ENTP>ESTP.yure: The question "Facts or ideas?" makes you waver. Picture yourself planning something new, and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself working on site, and you lean toward facts.
ENTP>ESTP.plus: You can act fast because you don't want to miss a chance. You know from experience that going to check is faster than just thinking.
ENTP>ESTP.tip: For big purchases or important answers, sleep on it first. If you still want to the next morning, it's not just impulse; you mean it.
ENTP>ESTP.hidden: Listening to a friend, do you ever see where things are heading and think, "If you did this, it might work"? That's your temperament's power to picture what's ahead. Use it at work, and you'll come up with ideas others don't think of.
ENTP>ESTP.hidden_s: Listening to a friend, do you ever see where things are heading and think, "If you did this, it might work"? That's your temperament's power to picture what's ahead. Use it in group presentations or the school festival, and you'll come up with ideas others don't think of.

ENTP>ESFP.title: You make the whole room more fun.
ENTP>ESFP.body: Even when rain cancels the plans, you turn it into a game night at home on the spot. Even if more people suddenly show up, you quickly change the rules, "Okay, let's split into teams," and get everyone involved. The people around you end up smiling too.
ENTP>ESFP.say: "I've got a great idea! Let's do it right now!"
ENTP>ESFP.do: Even on a day off with no plans, you text a friend, "What are you up to?", and end up going out together.
ENTP>ESFP.worry: Even when you want to protect the fun, you can't help pointing out something that doesn't add up. You pick up on people's feelings easily, so you remember the moment the mood fell flat for a long time.
ENTP>ESFP.karai: You're the one who said, "Let's just hang out for a bit," and you're the one having the most fun at the end.
ENTP>ESFP.aru: At a party you suggest a game you just thought of, everyone loves it, and before you know it you're the most excited one running the whole thing.
ENTP>ESFP.aru_s: At the class party after an event, you suggest a game you just thought of, everyone loves it, and before you know it you're the most excited one running the whole thing.
ENTP>ESFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks about new things with logic. Through experience, you came to value the fun in front of you and how everyone feels. Your mind that comes up with rules is the same, and now you use it to make everyone laugh. It makes you happy when everyone laughs at a game you suggested, so before you know it, you're running things while having the most fun of anyone.
ENTP>ESFP.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "logic or feelings." The result depends on whether you answer picturing yourself thinking up ideas or having a blast with friends.
ENTP>ESFP.plus: When you're really enjoying yourself, the people around you feel like they can enjoy themselves too. Being able to brighten the room is a good thing about you.
ENTP>ESFP.tip: When a game is a hit, decide right then: "When are we doing this again?" If you set it while everyone's in a good mood, the next plan comes together easily.
ENTP>ESFP.hidden: When you hear a friend's plan, do you notice right away, "You won't have enough time for that"? That's your temperament's power to think with logic. Use it too, and people will see you as more than fun; they'll see you as reliable.
